To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the power conditioning circuitry is the most critical component of the energy harvesting system.

a) for a given harvester, there are a number of different power conditioning topologies, each with its own advantages and disadvantages, b) there are a number ways of managing the power from a given power conditioning topology, and c) the choice of power conditioning topology and management scheme depends on the application requirements and the available energy harvesting source.

the most efficient and effective power conditioning techniques are the ones with the lowest quiescent power, the lowest startup threshold, the highest efficiency at the maximum output power, and the highest utilization of the harvesting source.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of low-power energy harvesting systems that are capable of powering low-power wireless sensor networks (WSNs).
the development of low-power, high-efficiency, high-reliability, low-cost, and small-sized power conditioning techniques for energy harvesting systems.
the power conditioning of kinetic energy harvesters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

no single technique has emerged as a universal solution to all energy harvester conditioning problems, and that the optimum solution depends on the particular harvester, the application, and the required performance.
the best solution for a given application is dependent on the requirements of the application and the energy harvester.
the best power conditioning solution depends on the application and the available technology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy harvester is a power source that can be used to power low-power systems.

the energy harvesting system should have a low quiescent power and a low startup threshold, but should not be optimized for efficiency, and that a high utilization is possible with a low-power management system.

the power conditioning techniques are not well suited to the low-power applications of interest and that there is a need for more work on the design of power conditioning circuitry for low-power kinetic energy harvesting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power conditioning circuitry must be carefully designed to maximize the utilization of the harvesting source, which in most cases will require some level of power management.

the power conditioning stage is a critical component of the overall energy harvesting system, and that it should be designed with careful consideration of the harvester characteristics and application constraints.
power conditioning techniques are a critical part of energy harvesting systems, and their design is often overlooked.
